overview: NagaCorp Ltd. is the largest integrated resort operator in Cambodia, listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange since 2006. Its flagship property, NagaWorld, is Phnom Penh's only integrated hotel, casino and entertainment complex, operated under a 70-year casino license running to 2065 and an exclusive right to operate casinos within a 200-km radius of Phnom Penh (with limited carve-outs) until 2045. Revenue is reported in US dollars and is overwhelmingly derived from gaming (mass market tables, electronic gaming machines, and VIP rolling programs), supplemented by hotel, food & beverage and entertainment operations, with a long-dormant Vladivostok, Russia gaming project and a planned Naga3 expansion as optionality beyond the core Phnom Penh asset.

business_model.summary: NagaCorp earns the large majority of revenue from casino gross gaming revenue (GGR) at NagaWorld, split between Mass Market (public floor tables and electronic gaming machines, serving walk-in/local and regional visitors) and VIP (Premium VIP, direct cash-funded high rollers; and Referral VIP, agent/junket-introduced players), plus a smaller non-gaming hospitality segment (hotel rooms, F&B, entertainment). FY2025 GGR was US$691.6 million and net gaming revenue US$611.0 million, with Mass Market Tables + EGM contributing roughly 68% of GGR and the two VIP channels roughly 30%; Mass Market plus Premium VIP together account for ~90% of total GGR and gross profit. The business is transactional/volume-driven (buy-ins, bills-in and rollings multiplied by win rate) rather than subscription-based, with a loyalty program (NagaWorld Rewards) used to drive repeat visitation and cross-sell non-gaming spend.
business_model.customer_type: B2C consumer gaming/leisure (mass market walk-in and expatriate/regional visitors) plus a smaller high-net-worth VIP clientele accessed directly or through referral/junket agents; largely cash-funded rather than credit-extended
business_model.geographic_mix: Single-site concentration: substantially all revenue generated at NagaWorld in Phnom Penh, Cambodia; customer base drawn from Cambodia's resident/expatriate 'Greater City' population, ASEAN visitors, and international (notably Chinese) tourists and business travelers; reporting currency USD

main_competitors: Border-area Cambodian casinos (Poipet, Bavet, Koh Kong) serving Thai/Vietnamese cross-border traffic
Macau operators (Sands China, Galaxy, Wynn Macau, MGM China, SJM, Melco) for regional VIP/premium mass
Philippine integrated resorts (Solaire/Bloomberry, City of Dreams Manila/Melco, Okada Manila)
Vietnam casinos (Corona Resort & Casino Phu Quoc, Hoiana) targeting regional and Chinese visitors
Singapore integrated resorts (Marina Bay Sands, Resorts World Sentosa) for premium Asian gaming demand
Vladivostok/Primorye casino cluster (Tigre de Cristal) for Russian/Northeast Asian gaming demand
competitive_position.market_position: Monopoly operator within Phnom Penh and a 200-km radius under an exclusive, government-granted casino concession; the dominant, and effectively only, large-scale integrated resort serving Cambodia's capital region

moat_factors.description: 70-year casino license to 2065 plus an exclusive right to operate casinos within 200km of Phnom Penh until 2045 creates a legally protected monopoly over the capital's gaming market

NagaWorld is Phnom Penh's only integrated hotel and entertainment complex, with an established, diversified property (Naga1/Naga2) that has decades of accumulated customer relationships and brand recognition, including the longest operating track record as Cambodia's original listed gaming company
Longstanding ties to the Royal Government of Cambodia and alignment with national tourism/FDI strategy support continued operating stability, though this cuts both ways as a source of political risk

Management cites industry-leading profitability margins (FY2025 gross margin ~81%, EBITDA margin ~57%) versus regional peers, reflecting the low-competition, favorable-cost Cambodian operating environment

weaknesses: Single-asset, single-country concentration -- essentially 100% of cash-generating operations tied to one property in one jurisdiction

Heavy reliance on cross-border and Chinese visitation/junket flows that are exposed to geopolitical disruption (e.g., 2025-2026 Thailand-Cambodia border conflict, China outbound travel policy, scam-center reputational overhang)
VIP segment economics depend on third-party referral/junket agents, introducing counterparty, reputational and AML/compliance risk inherent to the junket model industry-wide
Limited diversification versus larger regional peers (Macau, Singapore, Philippines operators with multiple properties/markets)
Perceived governance/transparency discount typical of Cambodia-domiciled, founder-controlled gaming companies

growth_drivers: Continued post-COVID recovery of Cambodia's international tourism and business travel (2025 international arrivals at ~84% of 2019 pre-pandemic levels; Mass Market volumes already above 2019 levels)
New Techo International Airport (opened September 2025, serving up to 15m passengers/yr rising to 50m by 2050) expanding air connectivity and visitor capacity to Phnom Penh

"Cambodia-China Tourism Year" initiatives, visa-fee reductions, and a four-month Chinese visa exemption trial (mid-2026) aimed at reviving Chinese arrivals, which grew ~41.5% YoY in FY2025 and continued rising in 1H2026
Premium Mass and high-limit table rollout, side-bet game introductions and loyalty-program-driven yield management lifting win rates and average spend
Growing "Greater City" expatriate/resident population in Phnom Penh providing a structurally growing, less cyclical mass-market customer base
Rising Cambodian FDI inflows (US$10bn in 2025, +45% YoY; China ~54% of FDI) supporting business travel and migration into Phnom Penh

Naga3 expansion -- though delayed to September 2029 and subject to a reduced/resized scope after the December 2025 termination of the original US$1.75-3.5bn third-party funding agreement, it remains a longer-dated capacity/optionality driver funded primarily from internally generated cash flow
Rising Southbound Stock Connect ownership (the only foreign gaming operator eligible) gradually broadening the Mainland Chinese investor base and share liquidity

business.description: All material gaming/hospitality revenue is generated from one integrated resort in Phnom Penh; any site-specific disruption (fire, labor action, infrastructure) or Cambodia-specific shock directly hits the entire business

business.risk: VIP rolling volume and junket volatility
business.description: Premium and Referral VIP revenue depend on large, lumpy rolling volumes and win rates that can swing sharply quarter to quarter (1H2026 VIP volumes fell versus 1H2025 on weaker business travel/cross-border sentiment); the Referral VIP channel's dependence on third-party agents adds counterparty and reputational risk common to the regional junket model

The original third-party funding agreement (targeted to fund roughly half of a multi-billion-dollar expansion) was mutually terminated in December 2025 with a US$316m advance forfeited to reserves; completion has already been pushed from September 2025 to September 2029 and management is reconsidering project scale, creating execution and capital-allocation uncertainty

The Group recognized an US$89.1 million non-cash impairment on its Vladivostok, Russia gaming project in FY2024; the project remains largely dormant pending further investment decisions and is exposed to Russia-specific sanctions/geopolitical and currency risk
Macau liberalization/recovery, Vietnam, Philippine and Singapore integrated resorts compete for the same regional Chinese/ASEAN gaming tourist pool

financial.description: The Group resumed a cash dividend (30% payout ratio) in FY2025/1H2026 while still carrying a long-dated Naga3 commitment to be funded primarily from internal cash flow, creating a trade-off between shareholder returns and growth investment

The now-terminated Naga3 subscription agreement was with a party linked to the Company's founder; such related-party financing structures warrant governance scrutiny even where legally structured at arm's length

Although income and most costs are USD-denominated (limiting FX transaction risk per management), a portion of costs are in Cambodian Riel and Russian Rubles, and the stock trades in HKD, introducing a reporting-currency/quote mismatch for HK-based investors

regulatory.risk: Cambodian gaming law and concession terms
regulatory.description: Cambodia's Casino Law and MOEF administrative practice govern gaming and non-gaming obligation payments; contingent liabilities exist around historical obligation payments subject to future government instruction, and any adverse change to license terms, taxation or concession scope would directly impair the core moat

The Group engages an independent reviewer on a semi-annual basis specifically to assess AML internal controls, reflecting heightened regulatory and reputational focus on Cambodia's casino/junket sector following US and UK sanctions (October 2025) against Cambodia's Prince Group/Chen Zhi network over cyber-scam and money-laundering operations; while NagaCorp has not been named in these sanctions, the broader scrutiny of Cambodia's gaming-adjacent industry and cross-border junket flows represents an ongoing reputational and compliance overhang for all Cambodian gaming operators

regulatory.risk: Cross-border travel and visa policy risk
regulatory.description: Visitor flows, especially VIP and Chinese tourism, are sensitive to shifts in visa policy, outbound travel restrictions, and bilateral agreements between Cambodia, China, Thailand and ASEAN states

macro.description: Renewed border clashes from mid-2025 into December 2025 (including reported artillery damage to casinos in Oddar Meanchey province) depressed sentiment and share price, disrupted regional air travel and cross-border visitation, and contributed to a weaker VIP segment in 1H2026; the situation remains a live, recurring source of volatility

macro.risk: Global and regional travel demand sensitivity
macro.description: International tourist arrivals, business travel and premium VIP spend are discretionary and sensitive to global economic uncertainty, fuel/airfare costs, and geopolitical shocks (management cited higher fuel prices and scam-center-related travel caution as headwinds in 1H2026)

macro.risk: China outbound travel and economic policy
macro.description: China remains Cambodia's largest source market (~26% of international arrivals in 1H2026); Chinese macro conditions, outbound travel policy and consumer sentiment materially affect both Mass Market and VIP revenue

Operations are entirely dependent on the continued political stability and policy direction of the Royal Government of Cambodia; the Company engages an independent consultancy (Political and Economic Risk Consultancy, Ltd.) specifically to assess Cambodia investment risk, underscoring this as a recognized structural risk factor

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Regional Asian gaming/integrated-resort demand continues a multi-year post-COVID recovery, with Macau, Singapore, the Philippines and Vietnam all competing for returning Chinese and ASEAN visitation; Cambodia's tourism sector was at roughly 84% of 2019 pre-pandemic international arrivals in FY2025 and is targeted to continue recovering, aided by new airport infrastructure and visa facilitation, though growth has moderated in 2026 amid regional geopolitical tension
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderately cyclical and sensitive to discretionary travel/leisure spending; the VIP segment is materially more volatile than the Mass Market segment, which benefits from a structurally growing resident/expatriate customer base that cushions overall volatility
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity given the Group holds net cash (cash and bank balances exceeded total debt as of 31 December 2025) and minimal finance costs (~US$0.6 million in FY2025, related to a shareholder loan and lease liabilities); indirect sensitivity via global financial conditions affecting travel demand and FDI into Cambodia
key_input_costs: Fuel/airfare costs affecting visitor travel economics
Casino license and gaming/non-gaming obligation payments to the Cambodian Ministry of Economy and Finance
Construction/materials costs for the Naga3 expansion

recent_developments.event: US Treasury (OFAC) and UK sanctioned Cambodia's Prince Group and its chairman Chen Zhi over alleged forced-labor cyber-scam compounds and money laundering; while NagaCorp was not named, the action intensified regulatory and reputational scrutiny of Cambodia's broader gaming/junket ecosystem and weighed on sentiment toward Cambodian gaming names

Renewed Thailand-Cambodia border clashes (from December 7) reportedly damaged several border-area casinos and caused NagaCorp's shares to fall over 4% on heightened geopolitical risk; Chen Zhi was separately arrested, deported to China, and had his Cambodian citizenship revoked in December 2025/January 2026

NagaCorp and the Naga3 funding subscriber (linked to founder Dr. Chen Lip Keong) signed a mutual termination deed ending the original ~US$3.5bn Naga3 subscription/funding agreement; the subscriber's US$316 million cash advance was forfeited to the Company's reserves, with no obligation to issue the previously contemplated settlement shares. Management said the termination would not materially affect existing operations or financial position and reaffirmed its intent to proceed with a resized Naga3, funded primarily from internal cash flow

Moody's credit commentary assessed Naga3 funding risk as manageable given the likely reduction in project scope and the Group's financial flexibility; Citigroup modeled a halved Naga3 cost estimate (~US$1.75bn) and adjusted its rating/targets accordingly

FY2025 annual report: net profit up 56.0% YoY to US$309.9 million (FY2024 included an US$89.1m non-cash Vladivostok impairment); EBITDA of US$404.4 million; revenue of US$709.7 million; Board recommended a resumed year-end cash dividend of US$48.3 million (30% of 2H2025 net profit)

1H2026 interim results: revenue of US$313.2 million and net profit of US$144.0 million, both down modestly from 1H2025 (US$148.8m net profit), as the Premium and Referral VIP segments softened on weaker cross-border business travel, geopolitical tension and higher fuel prices, partly offset by continued Mass Market growth and margin improvement (EBITDA margin, gross margin and net margin all improved YoY); Board declared an interim cash dividend of US$43.2 million (30% payout)

Thailand reportedly restricted its citizens from crossing into Cambodia to work in Poipet-area casinos amid border tensions, and Cambodia's broader tourism sector faced continued headwinds from the border conflict and international scam-center reputational concerns

items.notes: Resumed in FY2025 after a hiatus; continued at the same 30% payout ratio in the 1H2026 interim dividend (US$43.2 million), signaling management's intent to sustain the policy rather than raise or cut it

Originally targeted for September 2025; extended in June 2023 and further subject to project resizing discussions following the December 2025 termination of third-party funding; management states it is 'carefully and seriously considering options for developing Naga3 to match market conditions,' including resizing

items.target: Primarily internally generated cash flow; alternative funding to be explored if needed
items.notes: No longer reliant on the terminated related-party subscription structure; no specific capex figure has been reiterated publicly by the Company post-termination, though third-party analyst estimates (Citigroup) assume a reduced ~US$1.75bn total cost versus the original ~US$3.5bn plan

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman's commentary in both the FY2025 annual report and 1H2026 interim report emphasizes confidence in Cambodia's tourism recovery, the new Techo International Airport, Cambodia-China tourism initiatives, and NagaWorld's unique position as the only Integrated Resort in Phnom Penh, while explicitly acknowledging 'global macro headwinds and geopolitical tensions' (1H2026) and citing softer VIP segment business volumes due to weaker business sentiment, subdued international travel demand, and reduced international direct flights. Management reiterated an optimistic long-term outlook and a 'stable' near-term outlook, without providing specific quantitative revenue/EBITDA targets for FY2026.

bull_case: Durable, government-granted monopoly: a 70-year casino license (to 2065) and an exclusive 200km Phnom Penh gaming concession (to 2045) provide a legally entrenched moat with no local competitive threat through at least the next two decades

Strong balance sheet and cash generation: net cash position (cash exceeds total debt), ~57% EBITDA margin and ~81% gross margin in FY2025, enabling a resumed dividend (30% payout) while still funding growth

Structural, less-cyclical Mass Market growth engine: a growing resident/expatriate 'Greater City' population and recovering regional/ASEAN visitation already exceed pre-COVID (2019) volume levels, providing a more resilient base than VIP-dependent regional peers

Multiple tourism tailwinds: new Techo International Airport capacity expansion, Cambodia-China Tourism Year initiatives, visa facilitation, and rising FDI inflows (~US$10bn in 2025, +45% YoY) all support continued visitor growth into NagaWorld's home market

De-risked Naga3 optionality: termination of the related-party funding deal removed a complex, founder-linked financing structure and a forfeited US$316m advance strengthens reserves, while a resized, internally-funded Naga3 reduces execution and dilution risk versus the original US$3.5bn plan
bear_case: Extreme concentration risk: essentially all cash flow comes from one casino resort in one country, leaving no diversification if Cambodia-specific political, regulatory or infrastructure shocks occur

Geopolitical overhang from the Thailand-Cambodia border conflict, which has already damaged border-area casinos, disrupted cross-border travel and depressed VIP segment performance, with no clear resolution timeline

Reputational and regulatory contagion risk from the broader Cambodian gaming/junket sector following US/UK sanctions on Prince Group and Chen Zhi over cyber-scam and money-laundering operations, which could prompt tighter AML scrutiny, visa restrictions, or investor aversion to Cambodia-domiciled gaming names generally

VIP segment volatility and junket-model dependency: Premium and Referral VIP revenue (roughly 30% of GGR) swung materially between periods (1H2026 declined YoY) and relies on third-party agent relationships inherently exposed to counterparty and compliance risk

Naga3 uncertainty persists despite de-risking: the expansion has already slipped from 2025 to 2029, project scope/cost remain unresolved, and the Company must now self-fund or find new partners without the previously committed external capital
